result.question:
AUTONOMOUS DRIVING — outstanding research & engineering results from JUNE 2025 to JULY 2026, and how each could boost, combine with, or falsify the TanitAD programme. Restrict to CREDIBLE, HIGH-QUALITY sources (peer-reviewed, major-lab tech reports, reproducible benchmarks with public numbers). Reject blog hype and unreproduced claims; state evidence quality per claim.

COVER ALL OF: (1) data engineering for AD — corpus construction, balancing, auto-labelling, pseudo-labels, synthetic/sim data, scaling laws for driving data; (2) AI architectures for driving — end-to-end vs modular, VLA/VLM planners, diffusion planners, tokenisation, multi-camera fusion; (3) EFFICIENT INFERENCE AT THE EDGE for AD — sub-300M models, quantisation, distillation, CUDA-graph/TensorRT, Orin/Thor-class latency budgets, published ms/frame numbers; (4) evaluation & validation — closed-loop vs open-loop, corridor/safety metrics, statistical rigour, CARLA/nuPlan/Bench2Drive/NAVSIM leaderboards and their known pathologies; (5) THE LONG TAIL — mining, curriculum, rare-event synthesis, OOD detection; (6) best AI PLANNERS — MPC, CEM, diffusion policies, anchored/trajectory-set methods, learned cost; (7) efficient training with LESS DATA — pretraining transfer, self-supervision, curriculum; (8) unsupervised/self-supervised learning for driving representations.

OUR PROGRAMME (use this to make every recommendation concrete and testable, and to flag where a paper CONTRADICTS us):
- sub-300M hierarchical 4-brain latent world model (strategic/tactical/operative + fallback) over a from-scratch ViT encoder; deployed arm 286.3M params.
- Deployed v1 `flagship4b-speedjerk-30k`: ade_0_2s 0.4271 [0.3675,0.4871] on 881 windows/40 eps and 0.4108 [0.3956,0.4273] on 13,198 windows/600 eps, both CI-separated better than the constant-velocity floor (0.8377 / 0.6917). NOTE this metric is `wm_fidelity_ade_2s` — the world model is HANDED the expert's true future actions, so it is world-model fidelity, NOT planning.
- MEASURED 2026-07-29: pure imagination (camera cut after an 8-frame context, latent rollout) decays with a LOCAL exponent rising 1.03 -> 1.63 -> 1.87 -> 1.91 across 0.4-2.0s (ADE 0.0406/0.0829/0.1607/0.2753/0.4215). Near-linear early, near-quadratic by 2s. The >2s bound is ARCHITECTURAL — an index_select on the predictor's horizon embedding.
- Goal channels: substituting ORACLE speed (vt_band+vt_speed) recovers 0.1899 of the 0.2140 oracle-vs-produced ADE gap = 88.7%, entirely longitudinal (long_abs -0.3846 separated; lateral untouched). Route explains <=2.6%. tspeed_5s R2 0.7635 but RMSE 4.4545 m/s.
- Closed loop: CL-SFT cuts peak cross-track 38.944 -> 3.042 m (-92%) but every arm fails the open-loop non-regression guardrail; guardrail now gates lateral p90.
- IDM from monocular UNCALIBRATED video: speed R2 +0.865, yaw-rate +0.904 on PhysicalAI, steer +0.742; smaller is better (0.86M > 2.90M > 19.98M); speed is monocular-scale-limited, not capacity-limited.
- Corpus: PhysicalAI-AV, 2376-episode parity set; a 50h manoeuvre-balanced corpus (turns 14.25%->28.0%). SETTLED: PhysicalAI-AV contains NO map, lane graph, junction annotation or route signal, and egomotion has NO GNSS (clip-local metres). AlpaSim/NuRec DOES have a lane graph (12,030 successor edges over 11,877 lanes).
- Situation classification (lane change / intersection) from the front camera is above chance and anticipates by 1.4-2.0s, but does not beat an ego-kinematics baseline on HUMAN-DRIVEN logs.

DELIVER: a structured chief-scientist report. For every finding give: the claim, its evidence quality, the number, and a CONCRETE, TESTABLE measure for us — which of our hypotheses it would advance or falsify, what the cheapest discriminating experiment would be, and its rough GPU cost. Rank recommendations by (expected gain / cost). Explicitly flag anything that CONTRADICTS a result above — contradictions are more valuable than confirmations.
result.summary: Only four claims survived adversarial verification, and all four sit in area (4) evaluation & validation — the survey returned nothing admissible on data engineering, edge inference, planners, low-data training or self-supervised representations, so this report cannot speak to five of the eight requested areas (every edge-latency, planner-scaling, data-scaling and SSL claim was voted down 0-3). The surviving evidence converges on one thesis: displacement error does not certify driving competence, benchmark-SOTA closed-loop policies run on shortcuts rather than scene understanding, and the metric that does discriminate (EPDMS) is a multiplicative safety gate times a weighted quality average — a structure our scoring stack computes with an EMPTY gate product. The highest-leverage finding is internal and free: `pseudosim.py` refuses the collision gate because "episode->clip identity is not resolvable from the cache alone", but three later agents independently PROVED that join (600/600 val, 2376/2376 train, 40/40 eval-pod ids), so our only safety gate is blocked by a stale absence-claim plus an undownloaded chunk set — not by missing data — and fixing it unblocks both the safety gate and the free-space probe at ~0 GPU. Second: PlanT 2.0's positional-shortcut probe, which the verifier judged non-transferable to sensor models without a renderer, IS runnable on our stack today at zero GPU cost, because `pseudosim`'s `dpsi` axis is an exact camera rotation (max|dH| = 0.000e+00) validated to +/-12 deg — the lower edge of PlanT's 10-15 deg onset band — and the flagship already exposes explicit `vt_band`/`vt_speed` channels to plot against it. Nothing in the surviving set contradicts a TanitAD measurement: the one apparent contradiction (open-loop ADE is worthless) is scoped by its own source to nuScenes PLANNING, does not reach our `wm_fidelity_ade_2s` headline, and our arm passes the exact AD-MLP diagnostic that critique is built on.

findings.claim: The open-loop repudiation is REAL but SCOPED, and it does not reach TanitAD's headline. The Bench2Drive maintainers — against their own interest, on a NeurIPS 2024 D&B benchmark — call for the community to stop reporting and stop requesting nuScenes open-loop planning results, and state "L2 error is not a meaningful indictor at all". But all four occurrences are scoped to nuScenes open-loop PLANNING, and the technical document Bench2Drive endorses writes the limit down verbatim: the criticism "does not extend to other nuScenes benchmarks for perception and prediction tasks". TanitAD's `wm_fidelity_ade_2s` is by the programme's own definition NOT planning (the world model is handed the expert's true future actions), so it sits on the prediction/dynamics side of the line the source itself draws.
findings.vote: 2-1 (adversarial); quote verbatim-verified twice, incl. raw markdown
findings.evidence:
EVIDENCE CLASS: PUBLISHED (peer-reviewed benchmark, primary repo, against-interest testimony). Verbatim, README news 2025/02/05: "authors' should stop reporting results on nuScenes open-loop planning and reviewers should not ask for nuScenes open-loop planning results". Still live: README fetched 2026-07-29 retains the entry with NEWER entries above it (2026/05/21, 2026/03/27) — actively maintained, not withdrawn.

THREE REASONS IT DOES NOT LAND ON US, all from the source itself:
(1) SCOPE. The endorsed carla_garage document states "we do not claim that all conclusions drawn from nuScenes planning are incorrect" and explicitly exempts perception/prediction. Our headline is action-conditioned world-model fidelity, not a planning score.
(2) THE NAMED PATHOLOGY DOES NOT APPLY. The critique's mechanism is AD-MLP: a model that "solely extrapolates past movement" tops nuScenes planning. TanitAD publishes its constant-velocity floor (0.8377 / 0.6917) and beats it CI-separated (0.4271 [0.3675,0.4871] / 0.4108 [0.3956,0.4273]) — it PASSES the exact diagnostic. The other cited flaws (ego-status leakage, inconsistent metric computation, tiny val set) are nuScenes-specific; we evaluate on PhysicalAI-AV.
(3) DATE. 2025/02/05 precedes the Jun-2025 -> Jul-2026 window by ~4 months. The in-window anchor is arXiv 2605.00066 (Bosch, Apr 2026): L2 vs Bench2Drive DS Spearman rho=-0.36 p=0.43; NAVSIM PDMS rho=0.90 p=0.002.

ATTRIBUTION NOTE (cuts in the claim's favour): "L2 error is not a meaningful indictor at all" does NOT appear in carla_garage (closest: "the open-loop L2 loss can be misleading") despite being typeset inside a quotation attributed to it. It is Bench2Drive's own STRONGER formulation.

INTERNAL FLAG — the claim's own corroboration is unsound: it leaned on TanitAD's 0.45 -> 1.69 open-to-closed divergence, but commit f818a49 already retracted that ("our 'BOUND' verdict is confounded — and every CL number is a 2s number"), and that gap measures the PLANNER, not the validity of the fidelity metric. Do not re-cite it as confirmation.

CONCRETE, TESTABLE MEASURE (0 GPU, documentation only): in `MODEL_REGISTRY.md` and every report, rename the headline to `wm_fidelity_ade_2s (action-conditioned; NOT a planning score)` and publish the CV floor beside it every time — the floor is what defends us against the AD-MLP critique and it is currently not always co-located with the headline. ADVANCES: our right to keep reporting the number. FALSIFIES: nothing of ours. Note our own `tanitad_metrics.py` already cites 2605.00066 in its module docstring, so the programme has partially internalised this — the gap is presentation discipline, not knowledge.

findings.claim: EPDMS is not a displacement error: it is a PRODUCT of four hard compliance gates — No at-fault Collisions {0,1/2,1}, Drivable Area Compliance {0,1}, Driving Direction Compliance {0,1/2,1}, Traffic Light Compliance {0,1} — multiplied by a weighted average of five quality terms with weights Ego Progress 5, TTC-within-bound 5, Lane Keeping 2, History Comfort 2, Extended Comfort 2. CRITICAL CORRECTION the original claim omitted: each factor is filter_m(agent,human) = 1.0 if m(human)=0 else m(agent) — so an agent's zero does NOT zero the score on scenes the human reference also fails. Implementing from the claim's wording yields PDMS-v1 semantics and over-penalises arms.
findings.vote: 2-1 (adversarial); primary devkit fetched twice, identical content
findings.evidence:
EVIDENCE CLASS: PUBLISHED + PRIMARY, code-backed. Formula verbatim from docs/metrics.md on `main`: EPDMS = (prod_{m in {NC,DAC,DDC,TLC}} filter_m) * (sum_{m in {TTC,EP,HC,LK,EC}} w_m*filter_m / sum w_m). All four gate ranges and all five weights confirmed exactly as stated, all four gates typed "multiplier". INDEPENDENT ARITHMETIC CHECK: third-party 2026 papers report an EPDMS denominator of 16 (=5+5+2+2+2) and PDMS-v1 denominator 12 (=5+5+2) — consistent only with these weights. Not outdated: EPDMS/navhard is the live headline across 2026 work; our own `taniteval/taniteval/registry.py:272` already carries PDM-Closed (NAVSIM v2) EPDMS 51.3 as an EXTERNAL baseline.

THREE REFUTATION ATTEMPTS FAILED: (a) suspicion of a confabulated table — a second independent fetch returned the identical LaTeX; (b) hypothesis that Extended Comfort needs the two-stage perturbed-scene machinery (which would blow the cost estimate) — the doc defines EC as comparing "the trajectory outputs of subsequent frames and their resulting dynamic states", i.e. two planner queries at consecutive frames, implementable without scene synthesis; (c) no post-v2 revision changes the weights.

TWO FURTHER DEFECTS TO CARRY: full EPDMS also needs the two-stage pseudo-closed-loop protocol, reactive background traffic, traffic-light state, and a HUMAN-REFERENCE rollout for the filter — a lane graph is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT. And LK "is disabled on intersections where the centerline annotations often don't match the actual lane markings".

WHY THIS MATTERS TO US: it names the exact structural property our scoring surface lacks (see next finding) — a zero-factor that a good average cannot buy back. PREMISE INDEPENDENTLY STRENGTHENED by 2605.00066: ADE/FDE "exhibit no reliable correlation with closed-loop performance" while safety-aware PDMS correlates strongly "but with ranking inversions", the safety-progress trade-off being the source of disagreement — so the proposed experiment tests an effect already published; the TanitAD-specific magnitude is the novel part.

findings.claim: TOP RECOMMENDATION, AND IT IS A STALE-ABSENCE BUG IN OUR OWN CODE. Our scoring stack does implement the PDM shape — `pseudosim.composite()` computes (prod gate_m) x (sum w_x s_x / sum w_x) with gates=("no_collision",) — but the gate product is EMPTY, so the composite is explicitly refused the name Driving Score. The stated blocker is that `obstacle.offline` cuboids cannot be joined: "the cached episode_id is int.from_bytes(clip_id[:4]) and COLLIDES — 242 clip_index rows map onto the 40 val episode_ids". THAT BLOCKER IS STALE. Three later agents independently PROVED the join by replaying the cache's own recipe (sorted clip_ids -> split_clips(val_frac=0.2, seed=0)), reproducing 600/600 val, 2376/2376 train, and 40/40 eval-pod episode_ids with committed join_proof.json artifacts. The collision is resolved by restricting candidates to the known parity clip list. Residual blocker (b) — "the matching obstacle.offline chunks are not downloaded" — is a file transfer.

findings.claim: A benchmark-SOTA closed-loop planner's longitudinal target-speed output is driven by a spurious POSITIONAL cue, not scene understanding: rotating the ego by only ~10-15 degrees in an obstacle-avoidance scenario with oncoming traffic makes the predicted target speed abruptly jump to normal-driving values. The model "learns a shortcut by using its own rotation as a predictive signal for when the road is clear", and "once a decision is made to go around the obstacle, it ignores the scene and does not reconsider". This falsifies the inference that a high closed-loop score certifies a genuine speed/obstacle policy — PlanT 2.0 scores DS 92.4 +/- 1.7 on Bench2Drive (above Think2Drive 91.85 and every sensor model listed) WHILE carrying this shortcut.
findings.vote: 3-0 (unanimous); verified against raw PDF text extracted locally, plus an un-primed re-probe
findings.evidence:
EVIDENCE CLASS: PUBLISHED (Gerstenecker, Geiger, Renz — Univ. Tuebingen / Tuebingen AI Center; code, dataset and checkpoints released). Sec 5.4 titled literally "Positional shortcuts": "In all four scenarios, at rotation values around 10-15 degrees, the predicted speed abruptly increases to signal regular driving." Mechanism given: "the expert PDM-Lite only initiates a turn when the road is free. Since the dataset includes only correctly solved samples, the model learns to always complete an overtaking maneuver once initiated, ignoring potential traffic." Boxed Insight 4: "Shortcuts introduced by rigid expert demonstrations can be exploited and lead to unrealistic behavior." Verification was hardened: the first fetch echoed the query phrasing (hallucination risk), so an un-primed probe asking only for section headings independently returned the same finding, and the PDF text was then extracted and grepped at source.

FOUR QUALIFICATIONS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH IT: (a) PlanT 2.0 is a PRIVILEGED planner (ground-truth perception input; labelled "P" vs "S" in Tables 1/2) — "benchmark-SOTA" is true but is not a sensorimotor end-to-end result. (b) Root cause is CARLA-specific: a scripted rule-based expert plus a success-only dataset. TanitAD trains on HUMAN-DRIVEN PhysicalAI-AV logs with no "only turn when road is free" invariant, so a NULL result on our data would NOT contradict this paper. (c) The paper reports partial mitigation the claim omitted: "Although positional augmentation during training mitigates this effect, the model continues to be influenced by high rotation values." (d) The paper ACTIVELY CONTRADICTS the "transferable to any model with an explicit speed channel" clause: it chose an object-centric planner precisely because "it is time-consuming and non-trivial to perturb sensor inputs such as RGB images or LiDAR point clouds in a controlled fashion". For a general camera model that qualification stands — for TanitAD specifically it does not, see the next finding.

DATA-CENTRIC READING (secondary, and note the paper's own data-composition ablation was voted DOWN 0-3 in verification, so do not quote its Town13 numbers): the paper's remedy is richer, less biased demonstrations rather than a bigger planner — directionally supportive of our 50h manoeuvre-balanced corpus (turns 14.25% -> 28.0%), but INHERITED and not admissible as a decision input.

findings.claim: PlanT 2.0's probe IS runnable on TanitAD today at ZERO GPU cost, contradicting the verifier's judgement that it "does not transfer for free" to sensor-based models. `taniteval/taniteval/pseudosim.py` already ships a heading-perturbation axis that is an EXACT controlled ego-rotation on REAL frames — H = K R K^-1, "a pure camera rotation is exact for ARBITRARY scene depth (max|dH| = 0.000e+00, 30 conditions)" — exposed as `GridSpec.dyaw_deg`, with a MEASURED 0%-out-of-envelope span of |dpsi| <= 12 deg. The flagship exposes explicit `vt_band` / `vt_speed` goal channels (`stack/tanitad/models/flagship_v15.py:413,519,577`). Plotting predicted target speed against dpsi is PlanT 2.0 Sec 5.4, one-to-one, on an instrument we already built and validated.
findings.vote: synthesis this session (no adversarial vote); both components MEASURED by direct repo read, experiment NOT yet run
findings.evidence:
EVIDENCE CLASS: MEASURED (ours) for the instrument; HYPOTHESIS for the outcome.

WHY OUR VERSION IS STRICTLY CLEANER THAN PLANT'S: PlanT rotates the ego in a simulated scene, which changes the ego's world pose AND its object-level input together. Our `dpsi` warp changes ONLY the observed heading — the scene is bit-identical real footage under an exact homography. So if our target-speed head moves with dpsi, it is UNAMBIGUOUSLY keyed to heading rather than to scene content. There is no confound to argue about.

THE SHARP LIMIT, STATED HONESTLY: PlanT's discontinuity onsets "around 10-15 degrees". Our measurement-grade envelope tops out at |dpsi| <= 12 deg ("the widest grid that is still 0 % out of envelope"); `pseudosim` falsifies any |dpsi| > 12.0 deg. We therefore cover the LOWER edge of the reported onset band and cannot reach the upper edge as a MEASUREMENT. Pre-register this: a null result inside +/-12 deg is NOT evidence of no shortcut, it is evidence of no shortcut BELOW 12 deg. Do not let a null be written up as "we are clean".

CONCRETE EXPERIMENT (RANK 2 by gain/cost): sweep `GridSpec.dyaw_deg` across the full validated envelope on the 40-episode val cache with `dlon` fixed, and plot (i) the produced `vt_speed`, (ii) `tspeed_5s`, (iii) the longitudinal component `long_abs`, each against dpsi. Look for a step, not a slope. COST: ~0.3 GPU-day of inference on existing checkpoints, ~1 engineer-day of plotting; NO retrain, NO renderer, NO AlpaSim.
ADVANCES: directly interrogates our strongest measured result — that ORACLE speed recovers 0.1899 of the 0.2140 oracle gap (88.7%), ENTIRELY longitudinal, lateral untouched. If target speed is heading-sensitive, part of that longitudinal deficit is a shortcut, not a capacity or scale limit, and the fix is augmentation rather than a new channel.
FALSIFIES: if the speed head is flat in dpsi, it strengthens the current reading that our longitudinal gap is a genuine estimation problem (consistent with our IDM finding that monocular speed is SCALE-limited, R2 +0.865, smaller-is-better 0.86M > 2.90M > 19.98M) and closes off the shortcut hypothesis cheaply.
SECOND FREE RIDER: run the same sweep on the CL-SFT arm. CL-SFT cut peak cross-track 38.944 -> 3.042 m (-92%) while failing the open-loop non-regression guardrail — if CL-SFT is MORE heading-sensitive than v1, the guardrail failure has a named mechanism instead of a shrug.

findings.claim: The failure in current closed-loop driving policies is REPRESENTATIONAL, not sensory: models ignore obstacles unambiguously present in their own LiDAR returns and have not learned a general free-vs-occupied-space concept. TransFuser++ — the only camera+LiDAR arm and the strongest generalizer overall (67.5 HM on shifted routes, down from 80.8 in-distribution) — still fails to stop for a novel wall obstacle, and collapses from 33.15 HM to 0.00 HM in ConstructionPermutations when only the familiar warning sign is removed, i.e. the policy was keyed to a texture cue rather than to occupancy.
findings.vote: 2-1 (adversarial); every number verbatim-verified, but preprint with unpublished per-scenario n and no CIs
findings.evidence:
EVIDENCE CLASS: PUBLISHED-preprint (Gerstenecker, Geiger & Renz, "Fail2Drive: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Driving Generalization", 2026-04-09; open toolbox released; same lab as TransFuser/PlanT/CARLA-garage). Abstract verbatim: "ignoring objects clearly visible in the LiDAR and failing to learn the fundamental concepts of free and occupied space." Fig. 7 caption: "TransFuser++'s LiDAR visualisation shows the apparent obstacle in the LiDAR data and no bounding box prediction being made" — returns present, detector emits nothing, policy does not react. Body: "These large drops indicate that models do not reason about drivable space directly." NOTE the verifier's first probe wrongly reported the LiDAR check absent and nearly refuted on it — a textbook rule-2 single-location absence error, caught by a second probe.

THREE DEFECTS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH IT: (1) "0.00 HM" is partly a HARMONIC-MEAN FLOOR ARTIFACT — HM=0 whenever SR=0 regardless of DS, and per-scenario DS/SR are not published separately. Quote it as SR -> 0, never as a magnitude. (2) Per-scenario n is UNPUBLISHED in both paper and repo; the wall scenario's "4 out of 5 cases" implies n~5, and there are no CIs anywhere. By our own interval rules this is a DIRECTION, not a decision-grade effect size. (3) The appended "adding a sensor modality should not fix it" is the claim-writer's PREDICTION, not a paper result — the study is purely observational on off-the-shelf checkpoints, runs no modality-addition experiment, and n=1 camera+LiDAR arm cannot support a general modality-irrelevance conclusion. Strip that sentence when citing.

RELATION TO US: no contradiction — it targets closed-loop CARLA policies, whereas `ade_0_2s` 0.4271 is action-conditioned fidelity. It is CONVERGENT with our finding that CL-SFT arms trade open-loop for closed-loop, and it independently motivates an occupancy channel.

COST: <0.5 GPU-day, no retrain — but it is BLOCKED ON THE SAME episode->clip join and chunk download as the NC gate, which is why that fix is rank 1: one engineering item unblocks both.

WHY THIS RANKING AND NOT ANOTHER: every surviving claim points at the SAME missing capability — a scoring surface with a real safety factor and a latent with a real free-space concept — and both are gated on the identical join+download. Total GPU across R1-R5 is under 2 GPU-days on EXISTING checkpoints, against a survey that produced zero admissible evidence for any retrain, any new architecture, any quantisation target, or any data-scaling law.

Every claim that would have justified new training was REFUTED in verification: the anchored-vocabulary scaling result (1024->16384 anchors, EPDMS 85.02->87.35) went 0-3; the factorised path x velocity vocabulary went 0-3; SparseDriveV2-beats-diffusion went 0-3; World4Drive's self-supervised latent WM went 0-3 on all three of its claims; the dense-navigation lever (84.0 -> 85.5 PDMS) went 0-3; the Alpamayo edge-latency numbers (13.33 s -> 4.10 s on DGX Spark) went 0-3. Several of those would have been directly load-bearing for us — in particular the factorised lat/lon vocabulary, which maps exactly onto our diagnosed "5-way maneuver softmax mixes LAT+LON" mechanism and our 88.7% longitudinal oracle gap. THEY ARE NOT ADMISSIBLE AS DECISION INPUTS in their current state; they are re-verification targets, and re-verifying the factorised-vocabulary result is the single most valuable follow-up survey task.

GUARDRAIL ON R5: pre-register BOTH outcomes before scoring. If gated ranking agrees with ADE ranking, ADE-decided gates are vindicated for this corpus and we say so. If it disagrees, name in advance which decisions re-open — and note that 2605.00066 makes disagreement the EXPECTED outcome, so a flip must not be reported as a surprise or as an indictment of v1.

result.caveats:
COVERAGE IS THE BIGGEST CAVEAT, AND IT IS SEVERE. The research question asked for eight areas; four surviving claims cover ONE (evaluation & validation), with partial reach into architectures and the long tail. There is NO admissible surviving evidence on: (1) data engineering / balancing / auto-labelling / scaling laws for driving data; (3) efficient edge inference — no ms/frame number, no Orin/Thor budget, no quantisation or distillation result survived; (6) planners — every anchored/diffusion/vocabulary-scaling claim was voted down 0-3; (7) training with less data; (8) self-supervised driving representations — all three World4Drive claims went 0-3. Treat this report as a verified core, not a survey. Per CLAUDE.md rule 2, an absence found by one search protocol is not an absence: this may be a failure of the survey, not of the literature.

SOURCE-QUALITY LIMITS. Two of the four surviving claims rest on arXiv preprints with no acceptance notation (2511.07292, 2604.08535), mitigated by major-lab authorship (Autonomous Vision Group, Tuebingen) and released code/checkpoints. Both are from the SAME LAB and share authors — the two "shortcut/representation" findings are NOT independent confirmations of each other; they are one research programme with two papers. Fail2Drive publishes no per-scenario n and no CIs, its "4 out of 5 cases" implies n~5, and its "0.00 HM" is a harmonic-mean floor meaning SR=0, not DS=0 — direction only, never a decision-grade effect size.

TIME SENSITIVITY. The Bench2Drive repudiation is dated 2025/02/05 — roughly four months BEFORE the requested Jun-2025 window, and admissible only because the entry is still live on a maintained README. Its in-window corroboration (arXiv 2605.00066, Apr 2026) is a preprint with n=8 methods; Spearman rho=-0.36 at p=0.43 is a FAILURE TO DETECT correlation at small n, not evidence of no correlation. Do not quote it as proof.

TWO CLAIMS AS DELIVERED WERE MATERIALLY WRONG IN THEIR ACTIONABLE PART, and this report corrects rather than repeats them: the EPDMS claim omitted the filter_m(agent,human) false-positive rule (implementing from its wording gives PDMS-v1 semantics and over-penalises arms on scenes the human also fails), and asserted EPDMS is "computable ONLY on AlpaSim/NuRec" — false for the NC gate, which needs cuboids we already have on 97.44% of the corpus. The PlanT 2.0 claim's "transferable to any model with an explicit speed channel" is contradicted by the paper itself for general sensor models, though it happens to hold for us via an instrument we already own.

MY OWN VERIFICATION LIMITS. Every repo assertion here is MEASURED by direct file read this session, but NO experiment was run and NO eval executed. Specifically UNVERIFIED: that the proven episode->clip join actually resolves cleanly for the 40 val episodes in pseudosim's own cache (34 id collisions exist in the 2376-episode parity set; the join was proven by replaying the recipe over the parity clip list, which should resolve it, but I did not re-run it against that cache). Costs in the ranking are ESTIMATED. The upstream verifier also could not complete third-party contradiction searches for PlanT 2.0 (search budget exhausted at 200/200), so that claim rests on primary-source verification without an adversarial external check.
openQuestions: Does the proven episode->clip join (int.from_bytes(clip_id[:4],'big') replayed over the parity clip list) actually resolve cleanly for the exact 40 val episodes in pseudosim's cache, given 34 known episode_id collisions in the 2376-episode parity set? This is a ~1-hour check and it gates the entire rank-1 recommendation — the collision gate and the free-space probe both die if it does not.

Does TanitAD's target-speed head show a PlanT-style step discontinuity within our measurement-grade +/-12 deg dpsi envelope — and if the onset lies above 12 deg (PlanT reports 10-15 deg), is there ANY measurement-grade way to reach 12-20 deg without AlpaSim, or must a null inside the envelope be reported as strictly inconclusive above it?

Five of eight requested research areas returned zero admissible claims, and the refuted set contains results that map directly onto our diagnosed mechanisms — most sharply the factorised path x velocity trajectory vocabulary, which addresses the exact '5-way maneuver softmax mixes LAT+LON' defect behind our 88.7% longitudinal oracle gap. Was that voted down on substance, or on verification protocol? Re-verifying arXiv 2603.29163 alone is probably worth more than the whole surviving set.

If the gated composite re-ranks our archived arms differently from ade_0_2s (which arXiv 2605.00066 predicts), which specific past gate decisions re-open — and what is the pre-registered rule that stops a single re-ranking from cascading into a retroactive invalidation of decisions that were correct under the evidence available at the time?

refuted.claim: Bench2Drive-Robust (released 2026/05/21) is a public closed-loop harness that scores driving degradation under compute-control latency, camera-stream failure and ego-state estimation error — meaning inference latency is now measurable as a closed-loop Driving-Score cost rather than only as ms/frame, and ego-state error is a first-class perturbation axis (directly probing TanitAD's finding that 88.7% of its oracle-vs-produced gap is longitudinal/speed).

Bench2Drive changed its scoring protocol mid-life — adding Driving Efficiency and Driving Smoothness, removing the minimum-speed penalty from the Driving Score, and extending TickRunTime from 2000 to 4000 (2024/08/19 and 2024/08/27 entries) — and the current README still says baselines are being re-measured. Therefore Bench2Drive Driving Scores quoted across papers are NOT comparable unless the protocol version (v0.0.1/v0.0.2/v0.0.3) is stated.

NAVSIM v2's "pseudo-simulation" — augmenting real logs with synthetic observations rendered near the planner's OWN proposed trajectory, then re-scoring — is claimed to correlate strongly with full closed-loop simulation at 6x less compute. Evidence quality: PUBLISHED, peer-reviewed (CoRL 2025, Cao et al., Tübingen/NVIDIA/Bosch/OpenDriveLab/Toronto/Stanford) with public devkit; the correlation coefficient itself is NOT stated on this page, only the qualitative 'strong' + the 6x compute figure, so the number is INHERITED-from-abstract until the paper's table is read. FALSIFIABLE for TanitAD, and it directly attacks our closed-loop cost excuse: our CL-SFT arm cut peak cross-track 38.944 -> 3.042 m but every arm failed the open-loop non-regression guardrail — pseudo-simulation is the third option we have not tried (score the model on a small set of perturbed/off-expert observations near its own rollout, no simulator, no reactive agents). Cheapest discriminating experiment: take the 40-episode val set, generate K=4 off-expert perturbations per window around our produced trajectory, re-score, and measure rank correlation between this pseudo-score and our existing closed-loop cross-track outcome across the ~6 arms we already have. If rank correlation with closed-loop beats open-loop ade_0_2s's rank correlation, the guardrail should be re-based on the pseudo-score. Cost: no training, ~1 GPU-day of eval + renderer work; the renderer is the real cost and AlpaSim/NuRec is our only asset that can supply it.

The NAVSIM authors state explicitly that open-loop evaluation OVERLOOKS error recovery and deviation from the expert path — i.e. an open-loop displacement metric is structurally blind to exactly the failure mode a driving policy has. This CONTRADICTS the load-bearing position of TanitAD's headline number: ade_0_2s = 0.4271 [0.3675,0.4871] is `wm_fidelity_ade_2s`, computed with the expert's TRUE future actions handed to the model, so it is not merely open-loop — it is open-loop WITH oracle actions, one further step removed from the quantity NAVSIM says matters. It also independently corroborates our own measurement that every CL-SFT arm improved closed-loop cross-track while failing the open-loop guardrail: that is not an anomaly in our harness, it is the documented and expected divergence. Evidence quality: PUBLISHED (peer-reviewed motivation statement), qualitative not numeric. Concrete measure: stop reporting ade_0_2s as the program headline; promote a two-number headline (fidelity ADE + a deviation-recovery score) and pre-register that the guardrail may be REPLACED, not just re-thresholded to lateral p90. Cost: zero GPU, documentation + registry change.

The two-stage protocol scores stage 1 (the planner's trajectory on the real log) and stage 2 (follow-up scenes re-simulated from where the planner actually ended up), weights follow-up scenes by a gaussian kernel on distance from the planner's end position, and MULTIPLIES the two stage scores. The multiplication is the mechanism that makes the metric un-gameable by good average-case behaviour: a planner that ends far off-corridor gets its stage-2 scenes down-weighted AND its product collapsed. Evidence quality: PRIMARY, code-backed (official devkit docs). Directly testable against a TanitAD result: our imagination decay has a LOCAL exponent rising 1.03 -> 1.87 -> 1.91 across 0.4-2.0s, i.e. near-quadratic by 2 s, and our >2s bound is ARCHITECTURAL (index_select on the predictor's horizon embedding). A stage-2 protocol re-enters the model at its own end state, which is exactly the >2s regime we cannot currently reach — so adopting a two-stage score is BLOCKED on lifting the horizon-embedding cap, and that dependency should be stated in the registry rather than discovered later. Cheapest experiment: extend the horizon embedding (interpolate/extrapolate the index_select table) and measure whether the 1.91 exponent holds past 2 s or breaks; ~0.5 GPU-day of eval on existing checkpoints, no retrain if the embedding can be interpolated.

Training-data composition, not architecture, dominates closed-loop generalisation: removing Town13 (~40% of the training corpus) from PlanT 2.0's training set halves closed-loop performance on the CARLA validation routes, NDS 28.6 ± 2.9 -> 13.4 ± 2.9 (RC 90.6 -> 83.4), while the expert (PDM-Lite) sits at NDS 61.55. This is a direct, MEASURED data-scaling/composition result on a public closed-loop benchmark and is the paper's own evidence for its data-centric thesis.

Imitation of a rigid, deterministic privileged expert is itself the source of shortcut learning and of overfitting to a fixed trajectory set — i.e. the failure mode is attributed to expert/data properties rather than to model capacity or objective. The paper's remedy is explicitly data-centric (richer, more diverse, less biased demonstrations), not a bigger or different planner.

Closed-loop generalization failure is universal across current SOTA driving policies, not model-specific: on 200 paired CARLA routes with 17 held-out scenario classes, seven state-of-the-art learned models degrade by an average success-rate drop of 22.8% (average harmonic-mean-of-DS-and-SR drop 16.3%) relative to their matched in-distribution counterparts. Because each shifted route is paired with an in-distribution twin, the drop is attributable to the shift itself rather than to route difficulty. FALSIFIABLE: re-running any of these models on the public benchmark should reproduce the paired gap; a model showing <5% paired drop would falsify the universality claim.

Existing closed-loop AD benchmarks (CARLA Leaderboard, Bench2Drive) are pathological as generalization measures because they reuse training scenarios at test time, so a high score can reflect memorization of CARLA-specific recurring cues rather than driving competence. This is a concrete named pathology: models that score highly in-distribution (e.g. PlanT 2.0, SimLingo, TF++ all above 84 DS in-distribution per Table 1) still collapse on shifted twins, so in-distribution leaderboard rank does not certify robustness.

CONTRADICTS TanitAD's headline metric: across 19 public leaderboard submissions on Waymo's long-tail E2E benchmark, ADE and human-preference quality (RFS) diverge — only a mild positive correlation, with explicit rank inversions. WayNet achieves a top-tier ADE of 2.8 yet an RFS far below most models, while HMVLM has the WORST ADE in the reported table (3.071) but the second-best RFS (7.736). Waymo's conclusion is that 'ADE alone is insufficient to evaluate a model's true effectiveness in handling safety-critical, multi-modal long-tail scenarios.' Directly relevant to TanitAD, whose deployed-v1 headline is ade_0_2s 0.4271 and whose gates/guardrails are ADE- and lateral-p90-based: an ADE improvement is NOT evidence of a driving-quality improvement, and the CV-floor separation we report may not survive a preference-aligned metric. Cheapest discriminating test: re-score our existing 881-window/40-episode eval set under a multi-reference trust-region metric (see claim 5) — pure CPU rescoring of cached rollouts, ~0 GPU-hours — and check whether our arm ordering (v1 vs v1.6 vs CL-SFT) is preserved. If ordering flips, every ADE-decided gate in the programme is confounded.

SUPPORTS the sub-300M thesis with public numbers: on this leaderboard a 36M-parameter MLP/Swin trajectory model scores RFS 7.543 / ADE 2.814, BEATING the 3B Gemini-Nano MLLM baseline (RFS 7.528 / ADE 3.018) and matching the 3B AutoVLA (7.556), while a 60M DiffusionDrive-based model (UniPlan) reaches RFS 7.779 — better than every 3B MLLM except the winner. The entire 36M-to-3B range (~83x parameters) spans only RFS 7.528-7.986, i.e. ~6%. This is direct public evidence that capacity is not the binding constraint on long-tail driving quality, supporting TanitAD's 286.3M sub-300M budget and edge-latency posture. Testable for us: it predicts that scaling our flagship beyond 300M would buy <10% on a preference metric, so parameter scaling should be deprioritised versus the goal-channel lever (we measured oracle speed recovers 88.7% of the oracle gap). Note the diffusion-decoder result (60M > 36M > 3B baseline) is an independent second vote for REF-C's DiffusionDrive decoder swap.

Trajectory-anchor density obeys a non-saturating scaling trend in scoring-based planners: re-running Hydra-MDP on NAVSIM v2 with vocabularies of 1024/2048/4096/8192/16384 anchors yields EPDMS 85.02/85.80/86.33/86.78/87.35 (monotone, +2.33 total, per-doubling gains of +0.78/+0.53/+0.45/+0.57 with no rolloff), and 32768 anchors OOMs at >38.9 GB. Falsifiable and directly testable against TanitAD: our operative planner discretises with a 5-way maneuver softmax, which this result says is orders of magnitude too coarse and is a scaling deficit, not an architecture deficit.

The scaling is made affordable by FACTORISING the trajectory vocabulary into geometric paths x velocity profiles rather than enumerating whole trajectories: 1024 path anchors x 256 velocity anchors = 262,144 effective trajectories, described as 32x denser than the prior 8192 flat vocabulary. The ablation isolates the velocity axis independently of the path axis (512x128 -> 88.7, 512x256 -> 89.2, 1024x128 -> 89.5, 1024x256 -> 90.1 EPDMS), i.e. velocity-profile density alone buys ~+0.5-0.6 EPDMS at fixed path density. This is the strongest external support for TanitAD's measured longitudinal/lateral split — oracle speed recovers 88.7% of the oracle-vs-produced ADE gap, entirely longitudinal, lateral untouched — and it prescribes exactly the decomposition our single 5-way maneuver softmax currently collapses.

Dynamically generated proposals (diffusion planners) are NOT necessary for state-of-the-art end-to-end planning: a sufficiently dense STATIC vocabulary plus scoring beats them, with SparseDriveV2 at 90.1 EPDMS vs DiffusionDriveV2 87.5 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and 92.0 vs 88.1 PDMS on NAVSIM v1. This contradicts the prevailing 2025-2026 field assumption the paper itself states as prior belief, and argues an anchored/trajectory-set head is the cheaper high-value planner for TanitAD than a diffusion policy.

Existing SOTA end-to-end planners are effectively navigation-BLIND: on NAVSIM, corrupting or deleting the discrete driving command of Transfuser leaves PDMS statistically unchanged (baseline 84.0 vs 84.2-84.7 for none/random/left/right/forward commands, Table IV), and removal can even IMPROVE the score. This is a measured benchmark pathology, not a modelling opinion, and it directly bears on TanitAD's finding that 'route explains <=2.6%' of the oracle-vs-produced ADE gap: the paper's diagnosis is that the weak route lever is an artefact of the discrete-command REPRESENTATION plus a benchmark whose scenarios rarely require navigation-following, not evidence that global routing is intrinsically a small lever. Testable for us: re-run the goal-channel substitution with a dense route representation instead of a categorical nav_cmd and check whether the <=2.6% figure moves.

A denser global-navigation representation recovers a real, measurable planning gain that the discrete command cannot: on NAVSIM the navigation ablation (Table V) goes no-navigation 85.9 -> driving-command-only 86.1 -> turn-by-turn-only 86.4 -> 4x10 navigation path points + TBT 88.2 PDMS (+2.3 PDMS over no-nav, +2.1 over command-only); bolting SNG onto a Transfuser baseline lifts it 84.0 -> 85.5. This CONTRADICTS the reading that strategic/route input is a ~2% lever: the lever is ~0 for a categorical command and ~2.3 PDMS for a sequential path, i.e. the representation, not the signal, was the bottleneck. Note the dependency for TanitAD: SNG requires a navigation path, which PhysicalAI-AV cannot supply (no map, no lane graph, no GNSS) - AlpaSim/NuRec's 12,030 successor edges over 11,877 lanes is the only in-programme source.

World4Drive (ICCV 2025) is a peer-reviewed existence proof that a PERCEPTION-ANNOTATION-FREE latent world model can drive end-to-end planning competitively: nuScenes open-loop avg L2 0.50 m and 0.16% collision rate, which is an 18.1% relative L2 reduction and 46.7% collision reduction over the perception-free LAW baseline, trained purely by self-supervised alignment between actual future observations and observations reconstructed from the latent rollout. RELEVANCE TO TANITAD: this is the closest published analogue to our 4-brain latent world model and it removes exactly the supervision our corpus cannot provide — SETTLED that PhysicalAI-AV has no map, lane graph, junction annotation or route signal. It ADVANCES our core architectural bet. Cheapest discriminating experiment: add World4Drive's self-supervised future-observation reconstruction loss as an auxiliary head on our existing 286.3M v1 (no new corpus, no new encoder) and re-run the gate; ~1-2 GPU-days. Falsification criterion: if the reconstruction auxiliary does not move ade_0_2s beyond the episode-cluster bootstrap CI [0.3675,0.4871], the claimed mechanism does not transfer to our from-scratch encoder.

Discrete MULTI-MODAL INTENTION conditioning is the single largest ablation lever in World4Drive: adding intention alone moves L2 0.61 m -> 0.55 m and collision 0.30% -> 0.25% (Table 3, rows 1->2), and intention is represented not as a scalar command but as a k-means trajectory vocabulary of 3 command types x K=6 intention anchors. CONTRADICTION FLAG vs TanitAD: we measured that ROUTE explains <=2.6% of the oracle-vs-produced ADE gap while oracle SPEED recovers 88.7%, and concluded goal/route channels are a weak lever. World4Drive gets a large gain from a goal-like channel — but its anchor set is a trajectory vocabulary that jointly spans lateral AND longitudinal shape, i.e. it encodes the speed profile our route channel does not. This is a partial contradiction and it points at our own diagnosed mechanism (a 5-way maneuver softmax that mixes LAT+LON). Cheapest discriminating experiment: replace our discrete maneuver channel with a k-means trajectory vocabulary fit on our 2376-episode parity corpus, FACTORISED into separate lateral and longitudinal anchor sets, and re-measure the oracle-gap decomposition; ~0.5-1 GPU-day (clustering is CPU, one fine-tune arm). Falsification: if a lat/lon-factorised vocabulary still recovers <=2.6% of the gap, our 'route is a weak lever' result survives and World4Drive's gain must be attributed to its VFM priors instead.

World4Drive's latent world model is built on FROZEN LARGE PRETRAINED VISION FOUNDATION MODELS — metric depth from Metric3D v2 (giant) and semantics from Grounded-SAM — and the ablation attributes a large share of the gain to those priors: +Depth takes L2 0.55 -> 0.51 m, +Semantic takes it to 0.49 m with semantics specifically driving the collision-rate reduction. CONTRADICTION FLAG vs TanitAD: our deployed arm uses a FROM-SCRATCH ViT encoder inside a sub-300M budget, and our own REF-A result concluded a frozen-DINO encoder was a ceiling. World4Drive says the opposite for the *prior injection* pathway — the priors are not used as the backbone but as spatial/semantic supervision targets for the latent state. This also speaks directly to our MEASURED finding that IDM speed recovery from monocular uncalibrated video (R2 +0.865) is monocular-SCALE-limited, not capacity-limited: Metric3D v2 supplies exactly the missing metric scale. Cheapest discriminating experiment: distil Metric3D-v2 metric depth as an auxiliary target on our existing latent (teacher runs offline once over the 50h balanced corpus, no VFM at inference, so the sub-300M edge budget is preserved) and re-measure IDM speed R2 and the longitudinal component of the oracle gap; ~2-3 GPU-days including teacher inference. Falsification: if depth distillation does not raise speed R2 above 0.865 or shrink long_abs, the monocular-scale hypothesis is wrong and the bottleneck is elsewhere.

Optimizing NVIDIA's Alpamayo 1 reasoning-based end-to-end driving stack cut 6-trajectory inference latency by 69.23%, from 13.33 s to 4.10 s, measured on an NVIDIA DGX Spark with a GB10 Grace Blackwell processor and 128 GB integrated memory. The authors explicitly judge the residual ~4 s single-trajectory latency unfit for real-time use ("the inference latency for the single trajectory generation is about 4 s, which is not practical for real-time processing"). This is a hard, reproducible edge-inference datapoint: a fully optimized reasoning-VLA planner is still ~1.5-2 orders of magnitude off a 10 Hz on-vehicle control budget, on hardware substantially larger than an Orin/Thor SoC. It CONTRADICTS the implicit premise that reasoning-VLA planners are near-deployable, and strongly supports a sub-300M non-autoregressive latent world-model direction.

Sharing a SINGLE chain-of-thought reasoning sequence across all N trajectories does not measurably degrade open-loop trajectory quality or diversity versus generating one reasoning per trajectory: minADE6@6.4s is 0.743 (single-reasoning) vs 0.725 (multi-reasoning). This falsifies the widely assumed diversity-vs-efficiency tradeoff in multi-mode reasoning planners, and implies the expensive per-mode reasoning pass in multi-reasoning VLA designs is redundant computation.
